speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain. To help me assess your condition, have you noticed any specific triggers, such as food intake or exertion? REQUEST TEST: Electrocardiogram (ECG) to check for cardiac ischemia.

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Patient
text: point. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is surprising given your current symptoms; migraines do not typically present with persistent vomiting and chest pain unless there is a specific complication. Since I ordered an ECG, please hold on while I review the results to rule out cardiac ischemia immediately. While waiting, have you experienced any headache, visual disturbances, or sensitivity to light accompanying this episode?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Significant for Lyme disease, currently being treated with doxycycline. Social history: Reported alcohol use; found next to an empty bottle of vodka.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Alcoholic Ketoacidosis with secondary pancreatitis or myocardial infarction. Given the history of heavy alcohol use, persistent vomiting, and chest pain, I need to rule out cardiac ischemia immediately and check for metabolic derangements. Please provide the results of the ECG, Serum Electrolytes, Blood Glucose, and Lipase.
